question: The node row schema: you said 'something like json of metadata: payload: embeddings: and links: i think'. Measured today, cairn_nodes is node_id text (sha256 hash) / content text / provenance jsonb / standing text / created; embeddings, leaves and links are separate tables keyed by hash ids. Is a node row {metadata, payload, embeddings, links} as one record, or do embeddings and links stay separate tables addressed by row number?
why_it_blocks: born of the answer to open-b65577fa5584
answer: [message 1] the node has been envisioned as a record with one field (json) at one point, a record with metadata fields, and then everything was links to lists or blobs. it's specific contents need to be the node's state, it's payload (which right now is often going to be things like words for a word tree graph, or phrases, descriptions of design patterns, prose, blocks of text... but it can be anything. and to support that, i expect the easiest way is to also have a second table of rows, that is lists. like a list of links. every node and every leaf will have bidirectional links back and forth... so i guess my question would be: [message 2] nodes have to be fast, really fast. row ids are fastest. for lists of anything, we should stick with row ids. now that out of the way, a node's payload can also be json itself. or a csv block. so i'm thinking nodes point into a blob list or multiple blob lists. but given all that: how do you think we should do it? backing all the way up like joe bishop does with skippy, what's the most efficient and yet flexible memory schema we could build on these ideas for our overall cognition system? [message 3, after CC's schema proposal] i like it. one more thing, we'll need more metadata, a flexible metadata field. one of the first things in it will be a 0 to 1 "confidence" score. things we measure, like results of something, have very high confidence. things we read on the internet usually have a lower confidence score, depending upon the source. right now, we won't be using this much, but we will later. confidence will be treated like a why when making an ajudication about conflicting information.
